overall: Atlanta is starting the morning with a running max of just 78.8°F as of 08:50 ET, with temperatures essentially flat since midnight (77°F overnight, nudging to 78.8°F around 07:52 ET and stalling there). The atmosphere is very humid (dewpoint 71.6°F) and a low broken overcast deck (100% cloud fraction, ceiling only 427m/~1,400 ft) is currently suppressing solar heating — the pace of morning warming has been sluggish and deceleration (-0.9°F/hr²) is evident.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in moderate agreement in the low-80s range — ECMWF 81.3°F, NBM 81.9°F, HRRR 83.7°F — with HRRR running notably warmer than the consensus. The observed temperature is currently tracking well below all three model forecasts, and the very low ceiling at this hour raises questions about whether models adequately captured this morning's overcast suppression; however, summer convective cloud patterns in Atlanta frequently erode through midday.
max_temp_prediction: With a persistent low overcast keeping temperatures suppressed through mid-morning and roughly 5–6 hours remaining to the typical afternoon peak (~14:00–15:00 ET), meaningful warming will depend on cloud break. The META model (most reliable fusion) places peak probability at 84–85°F (28.2%) followed by 86–87°F (22.8%), broadly consistent with NWP consensus near 82–84°F. Confidence is below average given the 100% cloud cover and low ceiling introducing real downside risk; if clouds linger, ECMWF's 81.3°F or lower is plausible, but if they thin the HRRR-anchored upper range of 83–84°F is more likely.
